findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In S2 / the C4 proof, specify how surviving in-horizon events' authorship_ledger position.commit_sha bindings are rewritten in lockstep with their re-parented (new-SHA) commits, so verify-identity's commit-ancestry-scoped verification still resolves and enforces them under the re-anchored enforce_since.
evidence: Plan: 'in-horizon commits replay on top' and 'Per-ticket as-of-horizon SNAPSHOT trees are synthesized into one baseline commit; in-horizon commits replay on top.'
Ticket authorship_ledger entries embed position.commit_sha (e.g. commit_sha '3b868da48ebf...') and position strings binding an event to a specific commit.
verify_authorship.py: since_ref = cfg.identity.enforce_since — enforcement is anchored by a git ref/commit descent, so rewritten SHAs shift the descent set.
A rewrite changes every commit SHA (stated in Risk/rollback), so any ledger-recorded commit_sha for a REPLAYED in-horizon event becomes stale unless rewritten in lockstep.
findings.finding: The mechanism re-parents in-horizon event commits onto the new baseline (changing their SHAs), but the authorship_ledger records each event's position.commit_sha and enforce_since is a git ref; the plan does not close how surviving in-horizon events' ledger commit-position references reconcile to the rewritten commits.
findings.location: Mechanism S2 / Feasibility (rewrite primitive) / AC 'C1–C5 proven to preserve signature/authorship verification'
scenarios: A <N-day event survives the horizon, is replayed onto the baseline with a new SHA, and its ledger position.commit_sha now names a commit that no longer exists post-swap — verify-identity's commit-ancestry walk cannot locate/verify it.
enforce_since re-anchored to the baseline: a replayed in-horizon commit must still be a descendant of the new anchor for enforcement to hold.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the S3-backend CAS claim with ADR 0093's git-bundle-per-push representation: show concretely how a force-with-lease-style old->new tickets-ref swap maps onto the helper's bundle objects + 60s per-ref push-lock + merge auto-doctor (or state the S3 backend uses a different swap primitive and re-prove the no-lost-acknowledged-write property there).
evidence: Plan Feasibility: 'the same git update-ref old->new CAS ADR 0031 uses client-side on a bare ref; an If-Match / conditional-PUT on an S3 sync.remote backend (ADR 0093)'
ADR 0093:29-32 — helper 'stores the branch as git bundle objects under a key prefix'

ADR 0093:42-51 — 'one bundle per push', divergent bundle heads reconciled by a merge-based auto-doctor (folds every divergent bundle head into one by iterated lossless 2-parent merges), guarded by a per-ref push-lock (DEFAULT_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS=60)

Web: AWS shipped S3 put-if-match/If-Match conditional writes Nov 2024 — a real object-level primitive, but it operates on single S3 objects, not on the multi-bundle+lock representation the helper uses for a ref
findings.finding: The plan asserts the atomic CAS swap is realized on the S3 backend as 'an If-Match / conditional-PUT on an S3 sync.remote backend (ADR 0093)', but ADR 0093 documents that the git-remote-s3 helper represents the tickets branch as git-bundle objects (one bundle per push) under a key prefix — guarded by a 60s per-ref push-lock and a merge-based non-interactive auto-doctor — not as a single mutable ref object updatable by one S3 If-Match conditional PUT. The plan does not reconcile a force-with-lease-style old->new ref CAS with the bundle-per-push representation and the auto-doctor's lossless-merge semantics, leaving an unverified capability assertion for the S3 backend.
findings.location: Feasibility section ('an If-Match / conditional-PUT on an S3 sync.remote backend (ADR 0093)') and AC 'Atomic CAS-swap feasibility resolved across bare-git, GitHub/Gerrit, and S3 backends'
scenarios: A history-rewrite baseline swap on a data-residency S3-backed tickets remote where the operator expects the same atomic CAS guarantee proven for bare-git/GitHub/Gerrit
A concurrent writer pushes a new bundle during baseline computation on the S3 backend and the auto-doctor merges divergent heads rather than the swap failing a clean CAS retry

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the S3-backend CAS claim with ADR 0093's bundle-per-push + merge-auto-doctor model: cite the concrete atomic-swap primitive the git-remote-s3 helper actually exposes (or show one does not exist), and if absent, route the S3 atomic-swap feasibility to a SPIKE and state how reclamation swaps the baseline safely under the bundle model.
evidence: Plan: 'the same git update-ref old->new CAS ADR 0031 uses client-side on a bare ref; an If-Match / conditional-PUT on an S3 sync.remote backend (ADR 0093). ... This CAS primitive exists on every supported backend, which is the portability answer'

ADR 0093: 'the helper ... stores the branch as git bundle objects under a key prefix'; 'The helper stores one bundle per push and refuses ref operations when concurrent pushes leave more than one bundle for a ref'; 'rebar instead ... runs a non-interactive auto-doctor ... by iterated lossless 2-parent merges'; 'writes plain put_object calls'
No occurrence of 'If-Match' or 'conditional-PUT' anywhere in the repo (search_files returned no matches)
EVIDENCE CLASS: Contradicted for the S3 backend
findings.finding: The plan's S3-backend CAS assertion contradicts its own cited ADR 0093: it claims 'an If-Match / conditional-PUT on an S3 sync.remote backend (ADR 0093)' and that 'This CAS primitive exists on every supported backend,' but ADR 0093 describes the S3 backend (awslabs/git-remote-s3) as storing the tickets branch as git *bundle* objects (one bundle per push) via plain put_object, with concurrency producing MULTIPLE bundles reconciled by a merge-based non-interactive auto-doctor — there is NO atomic ref compare-and-swap and no documented If-Match/conditional-PUT ref-swap primitive.
findings.location: Feasibility section ('an If-Match / conditional-PUT on an S3 sync.remote backend (ADR 0093)'); AC 'Atomic CAS-swap feasibility resolved across bare-git, GitHub/Gerrit, and S3 backends'
scenarios: Reclamation attempts the atomic ref-swap against a project whose sync.remote is an s3:// backend and finds no CAS ref primitive — the bundle-per-push + auto-doctor model has no atomic tickets:=baseline conditional-on-T0 swap, so the 'no acknowledged write is lost / no hold-open window' guarantee does not hold as described

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the post-rollback reconciliation state: define what happens to clones that already reset/replayed onto the rewritten baseline when origin/tickets is reverted to the backup ref (how their tracking refs and replayed event files are recovered), and attach a literal DATA LOSS RISK note bounding any post-swap client work that cannot be recovered on revert.
evidence: Plan: 'Rollback: immutable backup ref refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-<date> before the swap; ... the swap is one revertible ref update'

Plan: S3 'stale-clone detection + forced remote-override on reconnect' and clients 'EVENT-FILE REPLAY onto the baseline (reset tracking ref, ...)' — clones migrate onto the rewritten baseline before any rollback

T11 POST-ROLLBACK-STATE clause: applies when the plan 'rewrites or migrates records in place' / 'performs a one-way transformation'; the plan must assert on state AFTER rollback, not merely that rollback completed
The accepted-loss statement is scoped to a '>N-day-drifted clone' at swap time, not to clones that already reset onto the baseline and must then survive a revert
findings.finding: The rollback design asserts only that the swap is reverted (ref update back to the backup ref), not what the persisted/interpreted state is AFTER rollback across clones that already migrated to the rewritten baseline. Because this is an in-place history rewrite (one-way transform of every commit/tree SHA) that S3 forces clones to reset onto, a post-swap revert to refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-<date> leaves already-reconciled clones anchored to a baseline SHA the remote no longer names and their event-file replays re-based onto now-orphaned history — a back-out that 'completes' while leaving fleet state incorrectly anchored.
findings.location: Risk / rollback section; Acceptance Criteria 'Risk assessment plus rollback (backup ref, shadow-branch stage) designed'
scenarios: Swap lands, several clones reset+replay onto the baseline, then rollback reverts origin/tickets to the pre-reclaim backup: those clones are now non-FF vs the restored history with local work anchored to an orphaned baseline SHA
A green-then-reverted cycle where post-swap client commits are silently stranded because the revert path has no defined reconciliation for already-migrated clones

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile 51a7's scope (.retired tombstone sweep) with the parent's proven lever (commit/tree history coalescing to a re-signed baseline), or add a child that owns the S2 history-rewrite/CAS-swap reclamation.
evidence: Parent: '.retired files are blobs; the guarded pack is blobless => .retired GC alone shrinks it by ~0. The real lever is collapsing per-event history into SNAPSHOT-anchored checkpoints'
Parent Mechanism S2: 'history coalescing to a re-signed baseline checkpoint ... Broadened from .retired-only to commit/tree reclamation (the object-count lever)'
51a7 description: 'The actual sweep that removes eligible .retired tombstones + folded companions ... only eligible tombstones removed'
Parent deferred S2: 'coalescing prototyped on a DISPOSABLE SHADOW CLONE ... two-clone resurrection test' - a coalescing prototype, not a tombstone sweep
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: Child 51a7 is scoped as a blob-level '.retired tombstone + folded companion' sweep, but the parent proves that .retired GC shrinks the blobless CI pack by ~0 and that the ONLY effective lever is history/commit/tree coalescing to a re-signed baseline checkpoint (Mechanism S2, broadened 'from .retired-only to commit/tree reclamation'). As scoped, 51a7 does not deliver the parent's object-count lever, so the parent's core S2 coalescing/history-rewrite execution is covered by no child in the roster.
scenarios: After 51a7 ships, the .retired tombstones are removed but the blobless CI pack (verify-identity.yml:47, 100 MiB budget) is unchanged (~0 shrink), so the driving bug defensive-buckskin-rhino remains unresolved.
The parent's S2 coalescing/CAS-swap/fast-import history rewrite is never executed because no child owns it.
findings.suggested_fix: Either rescope 51a7 to the S2 history-coalescing/CAS-swap execution (fast-import baseline checkpoint + force-with-lease swap + backup ref + shadow-branch staging), or add a dedicated child for the object-count reclamation and keep 51a7 as the (acknowledged low-value) tombstone cleanup.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign an owner for the <N-day-clone non-FF reconcile / event-file-replay-onto-baseline path (distinct from aff9's >N-day forced override).
evidence: Parent Feasibility: 'Clients then reconcile: a post-swap push is non-FF vs the new baseline -> rejected -> EVENT-FILE REPLAY onto the baseline (reset tracking ref, re-stage append-only local-only event files, commit); a >N-day offline clone loses divergent work'
Parent AC: 'C1-C5 proven to prevent resurrection across all clone states, incl. a <N-day clone with unpushed writes'
aff9 description: 'Detect a clone whose last convergence with the remote exceeds the N-day horizon and force it to override local state' - explicitly the >N-day case only
51a7/e32d/866f descriptions contain no client-side event-file-replay reconcile mechanism
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: The parent's client-side reconcile path for a <N-day (non-stale) clone with unpushed writes - non-FF post-swap push rejected, then EVENT-FILE REPLAY onto the new baseline - is owned by no child. aff9 explicitly covers only the >N-day STALE clone case (forced override). The parent AC 'prove C1-C5 prevent resurrection across all clone states, incl. a <N-day clone with unpushed writes' therefore has no child delivering the <N-day reconcile mechanism.
scenarios: A developer's <N-day clone with legitimate unpushed local event files pushes after the CAS-swap; the push is non-FF; without a child owning the replay-onto-baseline reconcile, the developer's acknowledged writes are lost or the push is silently blocked.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the client-side event-file-replay reconcile mechanism as an explicit scope item on a child (either broaden aff9 to cover both stale and non-stale reconcile, or add a new child), and cite it under the parent's 'all clone states incl. <N-day' resurrection-proof AC.

evidence: Parent Risk/rollback: 'immutable backup ref refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-<date> before the swap; stage on a shadow branch verified by rebar fsck + full-log replay + verify-authorship; the swap is one revertible ref update; never prune the backup until a green Verify Authorship Identity run'
Parent deferred S2: 'coalescing prototyped on a DISPOSABLE SHADOW CLONE (never pushed); fsck/replay/verify-authorship clean on that shadow branch'
51a7 description mentions a 'reconvergence fixture' but not backup-ref creation, shadow-branch staging, or CAS-swap execution/rollback
No other child (866f ADR, e32d read-only eligibility, aff9 stale-override) owns the swap execution + backup/rollback
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: The parent's Risk/rollback design (immutable backup ref refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-<date> before the swap; shadow-branch stage verified by rebar fsck + full-log replay + verify-authorship; single revertible ref update; do-not-prune-until-green) is not owned by any child. 51a7 mentions 'I1-I9 preserved on a reconvergence fixture' but no child owns the backup-ref creation, shadow-branch staging, or the CAS-swap-with-rollback execution described in the parent.
